newsitem.title: MEXICO: Zaptista rebels announce boycott of Mexican vote.
newsitem.headline: Zaptista rebels announce boycott of Mexican vote.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1997-07-02

text.p: Mexico's Zapatista rebels on Wednesday said Indian groups in four southeastern states had launched a boycott of Mexico's mid-term elections next Sunday.

"Indian communities, Zapatista and non-Zapatista, in the south and southeast of Mexico have decided not to take part in the upcoming elections," the rebel chief, Subcommander Marcos, said in a statement.

It was not immediately clear how widespread the boycott would be, but it was almost bound to include some 40,000 Indians who live in the remote areas of southeastern Chiapas state that the rebels call their zone of control.

Marcos said the other states were Oaxaca, Guerrero and Hidalgo, areas where the Zapatistas do not operate, and where another leftist rebel group, the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), is considered to have a stronger presence.
The EPR has called a unilateral ceasefire ahead of the vote to renew the 500-seat lower house of Congress and a quarter of the Senate, and says it does not oppose elections.

Marcos, who has recently appeared increasingly isolated nationally, said the boycott would be "a protest against militarization and the atmosphere of civil war promoted by federal and local governments."
The Zapatistas, who rose up briefly for Indian rights in 1994, are surrounded by the army in Chiapas.

On Tuesday, Jose Woldenberg, head of the supreme electoral body, the Federal Electoral Institute, told Reuters in an interview he had decided against installing 23 polling booths in Zapatista-controlled areas, considering them no-go zones.
